reasoning:
I have enough. Key findings:

- eligibility/rules.py: QUALIFYING_SCORE=60, PREGNANCY_QUALIFYING_SCORE=45, threshold_for(household), is_eligible(household, score=None, today=None) checks status=="active" and score >= threshold.
- vulnerability_score(household, today=None) in eligibility/scoring.py, capped at 100.
- Household.status: "active" | "inactive" | "merged".
- is_eligible accepts optional precomputed score param — reusable pattern.
- No existing needs_review.
- Note: "within 5 points of qualifying" — score >= threshold - 5 and < threshold. Edge: score 55 for non-pregnant (threshold 60) qualifies as near-miss; 56-59 too. For pregnant threshold 45, near-miss 40-44. Also note is_eligible uses >=, so score == threshold qualifies. Near-miss must exclude eligible households. Also inactive/merged households excluded (status != "active" → is_eligible False; ticket says active households only).

One subtlety: is_eligible returns False for non-active, so needs_review must check status explicitly to avoid flagging inactive households that are within 5 points.
